item.title: Denial of Deadline: Network-Driven Accuracy Collapse in Distributed Inference Pipelines
item.description: Inference systems increasingly combine a fast path that returns predictions within the application's latency deadline together with a higher-accuracy slow path that runs higher-compute methods on stronger, remote hardware, so its results can be returned on time and combined with the fast path predictions. item.title: Evaluating Fuzz Testing for Reinforcement Learning Agents
item.description: Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents are increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains such as robotics, autonomous driving, and drone control, where unexpected behaviors may lead to severe real-world consequences. item.title: Decentralised Consensus Learning Networks: SME Rotation Without Centralised Reward
item.description: Centralised reward signals dominate modern AI learning systems, but they impose a single external definition of correct or valuable knowledge. We present a decentralised, consensus-based multi-agent learning framework in which expertise emerges through peer validation rather than prescribed reward. item.title: Model Predictive Planner for UAV Navigation in Non-Convex Air Corridors
item.description: This work presents a motion planning framework for UAV navigation in non-convex urban air corridors. The planner is based on a mixed-integer tracking model predictive control formulation that enforces corridor feasibility and dynamic consistency within a single optimization problem. item.description: Marine life monitoring is limited by strict energy constraints, poor underwater connectivity, and the high cost of transmitting raw multimodal data from remote deployments. item.title: Moral Hazard in Multi-Agent Language Models
item.description: Cooperation can fail when socially valuable effort is costly, weakly observable, and mainly benefits others. item.description: Cooperative perception through vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication can overcome the inherent physical limitations of individual autonomous vehicles, such as occlusions and limited sensor range. item.title: A Comparative Study of MCP and A2A for Inter-Agent Coordination in LLM-Based Systems
item.description: Recent industry practice has seen the rapid emergence of agentic systems composed of heterogeneous, tool- and LLM-mediated agent components, raising practical questions about inter-agent coordination and protocol design. item.title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement
item.description: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has driven recent progress in reasoning-oriented large language models (LLMs) by enabling large-scale optimization. item.title: LabRobFail: A Benchmark for Robotic Failure Analysis in Chemical Self-driving Laboratories
item.description: The deployment of embodied agents in self-driving laboratories could accelerate scientific discovery, yet their reliability is constrained by the irreversible and safety-critical nature of chemical experiments.
